t: You're looking at Napoleon as Mars the Peacemaker, a colossal marble statue by Antonio Canova, standing nearly three and a half metres tall. Napoleon appears nude, in the guise of the Roman god Mars, holding a gilded figure of Victory on an orb. Canova made it between 1802 and 1806, and it once stood in the Louvre in Paris. In 1816 the British government bought it from Louis the Eighteenth and gave it to the Duke of Wellington. It now fills the stairwell designed by Robert Adam at Wellington's London home, Apsley House.
